key_insight: SchGen shows that PCB schematics can be generated from natural-language intent by using a semantically grounded code representation instead of geometry-heavy schematic syntax.
engineering_relevance: This enables more editable, automation-friendly PCB design workflows and points to representation design as a key lever for hardware-generating LLMs.
method: Encode schematics with editing primitives, relative placement, and pin-name-based wiring.
Transform the task from geometry-driven drawing to semantics-driven matching for LLM generation.
Build a large-scale prompt–schematic dataset using a human-agent pipeline over open-source hardware designs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SchGen outperforms alternative representations and even larger general-purpose LLMs on wire connectivity accuracy and functional correctness.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality and coverage of the new representation and dataset, so generalization to unseen design styles or edge-case PCB conventions may still require validation.
paper_title: SchGen: PCB Schematic Generation with Semantic-Grounded Code Representations
